transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~68 minutes
Attendees: Priya Rao (Redwood AE); Ethan Garcia (Redwood SE); Asha Patel (Cedarmark - CISO); Michael Wong (Cedarmark - Infra); Sara Lee (Cedarmark - Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Deep dive on Private/VPC deployment architecture for Cedarmark, focusing on network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling, and compliance mapping to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls.
- Discussed options for customer-managed KMS/HSM for key ownership, logging integration with Splunk, and audit log retention.
- Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, provide VPC diagrams and terraform snippets, schedule on-prem connector pilot.

Topics: network isolation; ingress/egress; NAT, private link, endpoints; firewall / egress filtering; KMS/HSM customer-managed keys; audit logs / SIEM; SSO/RBAC; compliance mapping

Transcript:
[00:00] Priya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we appreciate your time. Quick roll call - I'll hand off to Ethan who will drive the network diagram portion and then we'll go over compliance mapping.
[00:18] Ethan (Redwood SE): Yeah hi hi, thanks Priya. Uh so what I'm planning to cover is our private VPC topology options: single-tenant VPC with VPC peering, transit gateway option, and on-prem connector patterns for air-gapped setups. Also ingress egress controls and firewalling patterns.
[00:32] Asha (Cedarmark - CISO): Great. High level for us: we need complete network isolation, strict egress controls, and we require customer-managed keys for all PII at rest. Also we need audit logs shipped to our Splunk instance, and SOC2 artifact review.
[00:48] Michael (Cedarmark - Infra): And one note — our infra team uses a strict outbound proxy for anything that leaves the network, so any connector needs to work through that.
[00:56] Ethan: Understood. Quick question, Asha — is the outbound proxy TLS-inspecting or passthrough?
[01:02] Michael: It's TLS-inspecting for most outbound, but we can exception for mTLS flows if needed.
[01:08] Priya: Ok that matters for mutual TLS and client certs. We do support mTLS for the on-prem connector and can accept certs from customer CA or support mutual auth with our service certs.
[01:18] Asha: Can you outline the ingress model you recommend? We are not comfortable with any public-facing endpoints if possible.
[01:24] Ethan: Absolutely. For Private mode we deploy a private control plane in our customer VPC — option A is VPC peering to Redwood-managed service VPCs but peering means transitive access considerations; option B is transit gateway where traffic is centralized and you can apply egress/ingress filters; option C is a fully customer-hosted on-prem connector that initiates outbound-only connections to Redwood so no inbound firewall holes needed.
[01:44] Michael: Option C sounds appealing cause it avoids opening inbound rules. How does that work with large model artifacts? We need to know egress bandwidth and chunking.
[01:53] Ethan: Right — the connector pulls model artifacts on-demand, and we support chunked downloads with resumable transfers. For bandwidth, we can cap concurrency and use pre-signed URLs over TLS. Also if you want, the artifacts can be mirrored into your own artifact store behind your controls.
[02:08] Asha: About encryption ops — we require customer-managed KMS keys in our account for all persistent storage. Do you allow BYOK / CMK?
[02:16] Priya: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via our Private deployment. You can bring your own key (BYOK) or use an HSM-backed key in your account. We integrate with AWS KMS or on-prem HSMs. We'll expose the ability to rotate keys and audit key usage.
[02:29] Sara (Legal): For the DPA side we also need to confirm key escrow and whether Redwood ever has key access — that will be a legal question but from a product perspective, can we ensure zero access?
[02:38] Ethan: Product-wise, for the fully Private deployment with customer-managed KMS, Redwood does not hold key material. Access to encrypted disks is via wrapped keys in your KMS. We can provide architecture diagrams showing crypto flows.
[02:49] Michael: Ok good. Next, firewalling — we run stateful firewalls at edge and have strict egress whitelists. How granular are your egress endpoints? Do you require large outbound ranges or can you provide an ASN + IP list?
[03:03] Priya: We provide a list of IP ranges by region and can support peering or private link endpoints. For Private we prefer interface endpoints (PrivateLink) so traffic never goes over the public internet. We can also support fixed egress IPs if you use our Dedicated fabric.
[03:17] Asha: What about DNS and egress to model registries? We can't allow arbitrary DNS resolution to external domains.
[03:24] Ethan: We support VPC endpoints for model registries and S3-equivalent stores; DNS can be constrained, and we can use VPC endpoint policies. If you need, we can provide a private registry mirror inside your network to avoid DNS egress.
[03:36] Michael: There's also the question of KV cache and ephemeral storage. Are those encrypted and accessible only within the VPC?
[03:43] Ethan: Yes. KV cache is stored encrypted at rest, and in Private it resides in resources within your account or inside a dedicated subnet with restricted security groups. We also offer in-memory cache options that keep keys in ephemeral memory and never write plaintext to disk.
[03:56] Priya: One nuance — some names in our product docs refer to K-V cache or KV cache, sometimes spelled K V cache, so apologies if I swap terms during the call.
[04:03] Asha: No worries. On logging — we need audit logs for every API call, with user identity, resource, timestamp, and success/failure. Retention 7 years for audit logs but stored in immutable storage. Can you feed those to our SIEM?
[04:17] Ethan: Yes we can stream audit logs to your Splunk/Datadog/S3 via TLS syslog or Kinesis Firehose. Logs include token-level metadata, model version, and route. For immutability we can sign logs and push to WORM-enabled buckets in your account.
[04:31] Michael: How about latency impact when streaming logs? If we push every token-level event it could be high volume.
[04:37] Priya: We usually throttle token-level events in logs, and provide aggregated traces plus sampling. For regulatory audits we can enable higher fidelity for a specific time window.
[04:47] Asha: For SOC 2 we need control mappings — can you map your network controls to CC6 and CC7 or whatever the control ids are in our auditor's checklist?
[04:58] Ethan: Absolutely, we have a compliance mapping doc that ties our controls to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 clauses. We'll attach that. Note that for Private deployments, some controls are shared responsibility — we'll mark which are customer-owned (e.g., perimeter firewall) vs Redwood-managed (e.g., runtime kernel patches).
[05:14] Sara: Regarding SSO and RBAC, we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for groups. Role-based access must map to least privilege with admin/read-only/ops roles.
[05:24] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC in the Console supports fine-grained roles and you can create custom roles that limit access to specific models and routes. We'll show the default role mappings and the SCIM schema.
[05:36] Michael: For network egress to external model registries, we need to know whether connections originate from inside our VPC or from Redwood-managed services. If from Redwood-managed, that'll break our egress policy.
[05:47] Ethan: For Private we can run the model-serving containers inside your VPC (customer-hosted), so outgoing connections originate from your control plane. If you choose Redwood-managed Dedicated we can provide NAT IP ranges or PrivateLink so you can whitelist accordingly.
[06:01] Asha: Can you describe the on-prem connector flow again? We want details - which side initiates, ports, and how do you handle mutual auth?
[06:09] Ethan: Connector is outbound-initiated from your network to Redwood's ingress endpoints over TLS. It uses mutual TLS with either customer certs or certs we rotate. It tunnels gRPC over the persistent connection for control plane signals and S3-like traffic for artifacts. Ports are typically 443 outbound. For air-gapped sites we can ship an appliance or support offline artifact transfer.
[06:29] Priya: Note: sometimes our docs refer to the connector as "onprem agent" which may show differently in older docs — apologies for that mismatch.
[06:34] Michael: Regarding firewalling and IDS/IPS, do you have signatures or integration points for our intrusion detection?
[06:41] Ethan: We don't ship IDS fingerprints, but we can integrate with your IDS by forwarding relevant flow logs and providing audit events. For high security we recommend using host-based monitoring inside the customer-hosted nodes and network-based IDS at your perimeter.
[06:55] Asha: OK, about data residency — we need all processing for EU customers to happen in EU regions. Can you pin regions for the Private deployment?
[07:03] Priya: Yes, deployments can be pinned to specific regions. For Private and Dedicated we can provision infra in your chosen region and ensure geographic restrictions.
[07:10] Sara: On the legal docs, one question: will Redwood accept customer security questionnaire responses as part of the contract? We usually need a complete security questionnaire returned.
[07:19] Priya: Yes we can take that and our security team will fill it out. We'll also provide SOC2 report and ISO certs subject to NDA if needed.
[07:27] Michael: Any constraints on peering to our network? We use Transit Gateway heavily, so if you use transit gateway peering, we need clear diagrams for route propagation and no transitive access to other TGW attachments.
[07:39] Ethan: We can provide diagrams and provide route tables that isolate Redwood attachments. For peering we recommend using specific route filters and security groups to lock down allowed subnets.
[07:48] Asha: Do you support fixed egress IPs for outbound to external partners? We need to whitelist partners like credit bureaus.
[07:55] Priya: Fixed egress IPs are available on Dedicated with static NAT; for Private in-customer VPC, outbound comes from your NAT gateway so you control the egress IP. If you need Redwood-managed egress we can maintain a small set of static IPs.
[08:08] Michael: How do you handle patching and kernel updates on customer-hosted nodes? We need a maintenance window and attestation.
[08:15] Ethan: For customer-hosted nodes, you control the update cadence; Redwood still publishes recommended security patches and will provide signed images. For Managed nodes in Private, we coordinate maintenance windows and provide attestations and CVE reports.
[08:28] Priya: We're logging this as a note — patch attestation and signed images are part of our compliance pack.
[08:34] Asha: One more thing — can you provide details about role separation for ops vs devs? We need least privilege segregation to prevent data exfil via model prompts.
[08:43] Ethan: Console RBAC supports scoping by model and route and we have token scopes where you can issue tokens limited to read-only or inference-only. We can show examples.
[08:53] Michael: Operational question — if we run a pilot, what telemetry will Redwood want? We want to limit telemetry to non-sensitive metrics; raw prompt data must never leave.
[09:03] Priya: Telemetry is configurable. For pilot we can mask or exclude prompt text and only share token counts, latencies, and error rates. If you want to enable higher fidelity later, we can reconfigure with explicit consent.
[09:14] Asha: Ok that's critical. On audit logs again, can you supply immutable logs and chain-of-custody proof?
[09:23] Ethan: We can route logs to a WORM-enabled S3 bucket in your account, and provide signed hashes for immutability. That meets most chain-of-custody needs.
[09:34] Sara: For the DPA and security annex, will Redwood accept a clause for subprocessor listing and prior notice before changing subprocessors?
[09:42] Priya: Yes, we maintain a subprocessors list and give notice. We'll include that in the DPA.
[09:48] Asha: Are there any known limitations for PCI-level workloads? We assume not in scope for now but curious if any constraints exist.
[09:56] Ethan: We don't actively pursue PCI workloads in our hosted offering; for Private/on-prem with customer-managed controls it's feasible but we'd need to validate with our compliance team. We'll flag that as a legal/compliance follow-up.
[10:08] Michael: Can we get concrete network artifacts — sample security group rules, sample NAT rules, sample endpoint policy?
[10:15] Ethan: Yep we'll provide sample terraform and security group templates. They include CIDR blocks, SG inbound/outbound, and PrivateLink endpoint policies.
[10:22] Priya: Quick recap before we go to Qs: we'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts, detailed VPC diagrams and terraform snippets, sample SG rules, and propose pilot dates. We'll also provide the compliance mapping doc.
[10:34] Asha: Sounds good. A few quick clarifying Qs — can the on-prem connector be configured to only allow specific model versions to be pulled? We want to control model provenance.
[10:43] Ethan: Yes you can whitelist model IDs and pin versions. We'll include model provenance and checksums in the artifact metadata.
[10:52] Michael: One last operational ask: we want the ability to revoke tokens immediately and have revocation propagate across running sessions. How fast is revocation?
[10:59] Priya: Token revocation is near real-time for control plane tokens — typically under 30s to a minute to propagate. For long-running sessions we have heartbeat checks and can kill sessions if token invalidation occurs.
[11:13] Sara: On the legal timeline, we'll need SOC2 and DPA review in the next two weeks to sign pilot SOW.
[11:20] Priya: We'll commit to sending the security pack by Dec 10.
[11:24] Ethan: I'll share the terraform and VPC diagram by Dec 13.
[11:28] Michael: We'll gather firewall egress rules on our side and aim to send by Dec 15.
[11:33] Asha: Any blockers on Redwood's side for the on-prem pilot?
[11:36] Priya: No blockers, just coordination for cert exchange and network test windows. We'll propose specific windows after we send docs.
[11:44] Q&A short exchange / small crosstalk: (inaudible)
[12:02] End of recorded portion.

Recap / Action items (auto-generated):
